Lastly, I will be looking at how DTW metrics differ among states and if there are any noticeable trends in reporting/predicting.

Data processing

hsa_state = read.csv("../hsa_state_inc.csv")

Metric functions

discrete_frechet = function(P, Q, dist_fun = NULL) {
    # P: n x d matrix or data.frame Q: m x d matrix or
    # data.frame dist_fun: function(x, y) returning scalar
    # distance

    if (is.null(dist_fun)) {
        dist_fun = function(x, y) sqrt(sum((x - y)^2))
    }

    P = as.matrix(P)
    Q = as.matrix(Q)

    n = nrow(P)
    m = nrow(Q)

    # distance matrix
    dist_mat = matrix(0, n, m)
    for (i in 1:n) for (j in 1:m) dist_mat[i, j] = dist_fun(P[i,
        ], Q[j, ])

    # DP table
    D = matrix(Inf, n, m)
    Prev = array(NA_integer_, dim = c(n, m, 2))

    # initialization
    D[1, 1] = dist_mat[1, 1]

    for (i in 2:n) {
        D[i, 1] = max(D[i - 1, 1], dist_mat[i, 1])
        Prev[i, 1, ] = c(i - 1, 1)
    }

    for (j in 2:m) {
        D[1, j] = max(D[1, j - 1], dist_mat[1, j])
        Prev[1, j, ] = c(1, j - 1)
    }

    # DP recursion
    for (i in 2:n) {
        for (j in 2:m) {
            candidates = c(D[i - 1, j], D[i, j - 1], D[i - 1,
                j - 1])

            k = which.min(candidates)

            if (k == 1)
                Prev[i, j, ] = c(i - 1, j)
            if (k == 2)
                Prev[i, j, ] = c(i, j - 1)
            if (k == 3)
                Prev[i, j, ] = c(i - 1, j - 1)

            D[i, j] = max(dist_mat[i, j], candidates[k])
        }
    }

    # backtrack optimal path
    i = n
    j = m
    path = matrix(c(i, j), ncol = 2)

    while (!(i == 1 && j == 1)) {
        p = Prev[i, j, ]
        i = p[1]
        j = p[2]
        path = rbind(c(i, j), path)
    }

    # stepwise Frechet values
    step_dist = apply(path, 1, function(idx) dist_mat[idx[1],
        idx[2]])

    frechet_steps = cummax(step_dist)

    list(frechet = D[n, m], path = path, step_distance = step_dist,
        frechet_by_step = frechet_steps)
}

dtw_distance = function(P, Q, dist_fun = NULL) {
    # P, Q: numeric vectors or matrices (rows = time
    # points)
    if (is.null(dist_fun))
        dist_fun = function(x, y) sqrt(sum((x - y)^2))

    P = as.matrix(P)
    Q = as.matrix(Q)

    n = nrow(P)
    m = nrow(Q)

    # distance matrix
    dist_mat = matrix(0, n, m)
    for (i in 1:n) for (j in 1:m) dist_mat[i, j] = dist_fun(P[i,
        ], Q[j, ])

    # cumulative cost matrix
    D = matrix(Inf, n, m)
    D[1, 1] = dist_mat[1, 1]

    # initialize first row/column
    for (i in 2:n) D[i, 1] = dist_mat[i, 1] + D[i - 1, 1]
    for (j in 2:m) D[1, j] = dist_mat[1, j] + D[1, j - 1]

    # fill rest of matrix
    for (i in 2:n) {
        for (j in 2:m) {
            D[i, j] = dist_mat[i, j] + min(D[i - 1, j], D[i,
                j - 1], D[i - 1, j - 1])
        }
    }

    # backtrack optimal path
    i = n
    j = m
    path = matrix(c(i, j), ncol = 2)
    while (!(i == 1 && j == 1)) {
        if (i == 1) {
            j = j - 1
        } else if (j == 1) {
            i = i - 1
        } else {
            # choose minimum predecessor
            k = which.min(c(D[i - 1, j - 1], D[i - 1, j], D[i,
                j - 1]))
            if (k == 1) {
                i = i - 1
                j = j - 1
            } else if (k == 2) {
                i = i - 1
            } else {
                j = j - 1
            }
        }
        path = rbind(c(i, j), path)
    }

    # stepwise cumulative cost along path
    step_cost = dist_mat[path]
    cum_cost = cumsum(step_cost)

    list(dtw_distance = D[n, m], path = path, step_cost = step_cost,
        cum_cost = cum_cost)
}

Graphing and stats functions

graph_hsa = function(hsa_id = 688) {
    hsa = hsa_state[hsa_state$hsa_nci_id == hsa_id, ]

    P = as.matrix(hsa$inc_hsa)
    Q = as.matrix(hsa$inc_state)

    res_dtw = dtw_distance(P, Q)

    res = discrete_frechet(P, Q)

    normal = ggplot(hsa) + geom_line(linewidth = 1, (aes(x = seq_len(148),
        y = inc_hsa, color = "HSA"))) + geom_line(linewidth = 1,
        (aes(x = seq_len(148), y = inc_state, color = "State"))) +
        labs(x = "index (weeks, 2022 Week 39 to 2025 Week 30)",
            y = "infected_value (?)", title = paste0("Local vs. state inc values for HSA ID ",
                hsa_id, " from ", hsa$state)) + theme_minimal() +
        scale_color_manual(name = "Legend", values = c(HSA = "blue",
            State = "red"))

    frechet = ggplot() + geom_line(aes(x = seq_len(length(res$frechet_by_step)),
        y = res$frechet_by_step), linewidth = 1) + theme_minimal() +
        labs(x = "Steps", y = "Frechet distance", title = "Frechet distance by step")

    dtw = ggplot() + geom_line(aes(x = seq_len(length(res_dtw$cum_cost)),
        y = res_dtw$cum_cost), linewidth = 1) + theme_minimal() +
        labs(x = "Steps", y = "Cumulative DTW cost", title = "DTW cumulative cost along optimal path by step")

    # dtw adjusted
    P_warped = rep(NA, length(Q))
    i = res_dtw$path[, 1]
    j = res_dtw$path[, 2]
    P_warped[j] = P[i]
    # P_warped = na.approx(P_warped, rule = 2)

    df_plot = data.frame(index = seq_len(length(Q)), HSA_aligned = P_warped,
        State = Q)

    warped = ggplot(df_plot) + geom_line(aes(x = index, y = HSA_aligned,
        color = "HSA (warped)"), linewidth = 1) + geom_line(aes(x = index,
        y = State, color = "State"), linewidth = 1) + labs(x = "index (weeks, 2022 Week 39 to 2025 Week 30)",
        y = "infected_value (?)", title = paste0("DTW-aligned Local vs. state inc values for HSA ID ",
            hsa_id, " from ", hsa$state)) + theme_minimal() +
        scale_color_manual(name = "Legend", values = c(`HSA (warped)` = "blue",
            State = "red"))

    (normal/warped)/(frechet + dtw)
}
dtw_stats = function(hsa_id = 688) {
    hsa = hsa_state[hsa_state$hsa_nci_id == hsa_id, ]

    P = as.matrix(hsa$inc_hsa)
    Q = as.matrix(hsa$inc_state)

    res_dtw = dtw_distance(P, Q)

    res = discrete_frechet(P, Q)

    i = res_dtw$path[, 1]
    j = res_dtw$path[, 2]

    delta_t = j - i
    delta_x = P[i, 1] - Q[j, 1]

    stats_list = list(mean_abs_lag = mean(abs(delta_t)), signed_lag = mean(delta_t),
        lag_sd = sd(delta_t), dtw_mae = mean(abs(delta_x)), dtw_rmse = sqrt(mean(delta_x^2)),
        rmse = sqrt(mean((P[, 1] - Q[, 1])^2)), amp_ratio = median(P[,
            1]/Q[, 1], na.rm = TRUE), dtw_amp_ratio = median(P[i,
            1]/Q[j, 1], na.rm = TRUE), lag_amp_corr = cor(abs(delta_t),
            abs(delta_x)), frechet = res$frechet)

    stats = data.frame(Metric = names(stats_list), Value = unname(unlist(stats_list)))

    return(stats)
}

All HSA IDs metrics

I want to initially make two tables, one that holds HSA IDs and another table that holds metrics and statistics about their distributions from all the HSA IDs.

I tried running this with all 98,295 HSA IDs and that went terribly (took literal eons) so I’m going to use stratified sampling by state and go and get 10,000 IDs.

set.seed(77)

hsa_unique = hsa_state %>%
    distinct(hsa_nci_id, state)

state_sizes = hsa_unique %>%
    count(state, name = "N_state") %>%
    mutate(n_sample = ceiling(100 * N_state/length(hsa_unique$hsa_nci_id)))

hsa_list = list()
for (state_name in unique(hsa_state$state)) {
    state_subset = hsa_unique %>%
        filter(state == state_name)
    state_temp = sample(state_subset$hsa_nci_id, state_sizes[state_sizes$state ==
        state_name, "n_sample"])
    hsa_list = append(hsa_list, state_temp)
}
res = vector("list", length(hsa_list))

for (i in seq_along(hsa_list)) {
    ID = hsa_list[[i]]

    out = pivot_wider(as.data.frame(dtw_stats(hsa_id = ID)),
        names_from = Metric, values_from = Value)

    out$ID = ID
    out = out[, c("ID", setdiff(names(out), "ID"))]

    res[[i]] = out
}

dtw_results = do.call(rbind, res)

Using our stratified sample, we can now look at some key statistics.

metrics = setdiff(names(dtw_results), "ID")

summary = reshape(do.call(rbind, lapply(metrics, \(m)
    data.frame(Metric = m, Var2 = names(summary(dtw_results[[m]])),
        Freq = as.numeric(summary(dtw_results[[m]])), row.names = NULL))),
    idvar = "Metric", timevar = "Var2", direction = "wide")
colnames(summary) = c("Metric", "Minimum", "1st Quartile", "Median",
    "Mean", "3rd Quartile", "Maximum")
rownames(summary) = NULL
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(var_explain), caption = "Dynamic Time Warping Metric (+ Frechet) Descriptions and Significance")
Dynamic Time Warping Metric (+ Frechet) Descriptions and Significance
Metric Description Significance
mean_abs_lag Average absolute time lag between warped points Larger values indicate greater overall timing mismatch between series
signed_lag Average time lag between warped points Positive values imply HSA occurs later than State; negative values imply HSA leads State
lag_sd Standard deviation of time lag along DTW-warped path Larger values indicate more variable or unstable timing misalignment
dtw_mae Mean absolute error along the DTW-warped path (shape comparison) Larger values indicate greater amplitude mismatch after optimal alignment
dtw_rmse Root mean squared error along the DTW-warped path (large differences penalized) Penalizes large local mismatches, more sensitive to extreme deviations
rmse Root mean squared error along the regular path Baseline mismatch ignoring timing differences; comparison benchmark for DTW metrics
amp_ratio Median ratio of amplitudes along the regular path (HSA % of state) Values > 1 indicate HSA generally larger than State; < 1 indicates smaller
dtw_amp_ratio Median ratio of amplitudes along the DTW-warped path (HSA % of state) Values > 1 indicate HSA is larger than State along warping path; < 1 indicates smaller after alignment
lag_amp_corr Correlation between absolute time lag and amplitude warped difference Positive values suggest larger timing shifts coincide with larger amplitude differences while negative values suggest that larger timing shifts coincide with smaller amplitude differences
frechet Discrete Frechet distance (joint deviation in shape and timing) Lower values indicate more similar trajectories; higher values indicate greater overall deviation (leashed dog and owner, the Frechet distance is the smallest leash required)

dtw_results_long = dtw_results %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -ID, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

ggplot(dtw_results_long, aes(x = value)) + geom_density(fill = "skyblue",
    alpha = 0.8) + facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free", nrow = 2) +
    theme_minimal() + labs(title = "Density Plots for All DTW Metrics (+ Frechet)",
    x = "Value", y = "Density")

I think the most promising statistics are signed_lag, rmse - dtw_rmse (smaller is better), amp_ratio, and Frechet distance.

    y = lag_sd)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue") + coord_flip()

graph_rmse = ggplot(hsa_dtw, aes(x = fct_reorder(state, (rmse -
    dtw_rmse)), y = rmse - dtw_rmse)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue") +
    coord_flip()

graph_amp = ggplot(hsa_dtw, aes(x = fct_reorder(state, amp_ratio),
    y = amp_ratio)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue") + coord_flip()

graph_frechet = ggplot(hsa_dtw, aes(x = fct_reorder(state, frechet),
    y = frechet)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue") + coord_flip()


(graph_lag + graph_rmse)/(graph_amp + graph_frechet)
